papers.title: Waveform morphology links local circuit kinetics to cortical interactions
papers.summary: Combining neural mass modeling with human and macaque intracranial recordings, this study shows that synaptic rise/decay kinetics shape oscillatory waveform morphology and phase-dependent responsiveness, with local kinetics and coupling symmetry jointly influencing interaction measures and temporal irreversibility. In stereo-EEG from 23 patients, waveform asymmetry was most strongly associated with local irreversibility, while mean instantaneous alpha frequency was more associated with interregional measures.

papers.title: Slow-Wave Enhancement Reduces Axonal Injury in Murine Traumatic Brain Injury.
papers.summary: The authors adapted a weight-drop mouse model of traumatic brain injury to allow EEG/EMG recording and found that mild TBI produces cognitive impairment, EEG abnormalities, and diffuse axonal injury. Treatment with sodium oxybate during the first three days after trauma increased slow-wave activity and reduced axonal injury, whereas chemogenetic modulation of basal forebrain cholinergic neurons did not reduce slow-wave activity.

papers.title: EEG-Derived Proxies of Cortical Excitability in Epilepsy: Group Discrimination, Temporal Stability and Medication Sensitivity
papers.summary: Analyzing 1,404 scalp EEG recordings from 96 epilepsy patients and 85 healthy controls, this study evaluated eight EEG-derived markers of cortical excitability and found that only aperiodic offset and exponent showed FDR-robust group differences, with aperiodic offset higher in epilepsy. Both aperiodic measures were more reproducible across sessions in epilepsy, and higher antiseizure medication burden was associated with higher relative alpha power.

papers.title: Image-grounded encoding models reveal distinct temporal profiles of naturalistic object and scene processing in the human brain
papers.summary: Using image-grounded deep neural network encoding models to predict human EEG responses to natural images, this study found that models trained on object-bound features consistently showed a delayed temporal encoding profile compared with models trained on scene-bound features. The distinct encoding profiles were used to reveal the typicality of individual image elements as objects or scene parts, indicating differential temporal unfolding of object and scene processing.

papers.title: Spectral power and functional connectivity alterations in multiple system atrophy revealed by resting-state EEG.
papers.summary: Resting-state EEG and fMRI from 123 multiple system atrophy patients and 69 healthy controls revealed reduced delta power, widespread theta and high gamma increases, and decreased alpha/beta/gamma amplitude-based connectivity, with cross-modal fMRI consistency. EEG features correlated with motor/non-motor symptom severity, and interpretable stacking models classified MSA-C versus MSA-P subtypes and predicted UMSARS progression.

papers.title: Wearable sensing technologies and machine learning for fatigue assessment in sport horses.
papers.summary: A PRISMA-ScR scoping review synthesizing 102 publications (2015–2026) on wearable sensors and machine learning for fatigue monitoring in sport horses across five sensing modalities (HR/HRV, thermometry, IMUs, sEMG, GPS). It found that no single modality provides a standalone fatigue signature and that only a minority of studies used fatigue as a direct modelling label, most relying on proxies such as movement asymmetry or performance decrement.

papers.title: Development and EEG Assessment of a Virtual Reality Replica of a Prior Real Multisensory Environment Intervention.
papers.summary: Developed an immersive virtual reality replica of a prior real multisensory environment intervention and assessed EEG spectral and nonlinear features before and after exposure in 31 healthy participants, with the real-MSE data used only as a qualitative reference. The alpha/beta ratio (negatively correlated with stress) was the only feature significantly increased in both conditions, while in the V-MSE frontal theta and theta/beta ratio rose and relative gamma power and Lempel-Ziv complexity fell.

papers.title: Direction-specific effects of biphasic transcranial magnetic stimulation on cortical and cortico-spinal excitability.
papers.summary: Combined TMS with EEG and EMG in 23 healthy subjects to contrast biphasic pulses over left motor cortex applied in AP-PA versus PA-AP current directions at 110% resting motor threshold. AP-PA currents produced lower RMT and shorter EMG latency with higher N100 amplitudes, whereas PA-AP currents yielded higher mid-component cortical evoked activity and earlier P60, demonstrating direction-specific cortical and cortico-spinal effects.

papers.title: Invasive monitoring and mapping in epilepsy surgery: Acute and chronic intracranial recording from surface to depth.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
authors: Tatiana V H F de Oliveira
papers.summary: An ILAE Surgical Therapies Commission education review of invasive intracranial monitoring and mapping for drug-resistant focal epilepsy, covering the historical shift from intraoperative electrocorticography and subdural recording to stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG). It compares subdural and stereotactic approaches on coverage, mapping capability, diagnostic yield, seizure outcome, and morbidity, emphasizing that electrode choice should follow a stated anatomo-electro-clinical hypothesis.

papers.title: Syndrome-oriented CNS infectious complications after hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation and CAR T-cell therapy, part 1-viral encephalitis, meningitis, and myelitis: recommendations from the Practice Harmonization & Guidelines Committee of the EBMT.
papers.summary: This EBMT consensus review provides harmonized recommendations for definition, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of viral encephalitis, meningitis, and myelitis after HSCT and CAR T-cell therapy, proposing standardized diagnostic categories and an algorithm integrating clinical, neuroimaging, EEG, CSF, and virological testing. It highlights key neurotropic viruses for initial CSF multiplex PCR panels and recommends risk-based empirical antiviral therapy, though many recommendations rely on limited evidence.

papers.title: From Synapses to Circuits: A Systematic Review of How Developmental Ethanol Exposure Alters Excitation-Inhibition Balance.
papers.summary: A systematic review of 25 whole-cell electrophysiology studies (2000–2025) in rat and mouse models examining how developmental ethanol exposure alters excitatory/inhibitory balance. Most studies reported increased frequencies of miniature or spontaneous IPSCs, whereas EPSC frequency varied by brain region and developmental time point, and no consistent directional shift in E/I balance emerged, indicating more consistent inhibitory effects and circuit-dependent heterogeneity.

papers.title: Neurophysiological changes following intensive Naikan therapy in a patient with recurrent depressive episodes later diagnosed with bipolar II disorder: A case report.
papers.journal: PCN reports : psychiatry and clinical neurosciences
papers.summary: In a 29-year-old man with recurrent depressive episodes later diagnosed with bipolar II disorder, 7 days of intensive Naikan therapy was associated with decreased anxiety and depressive symptoms, reduced resting-state beta-band global field power, and increased P300 amplitude, though sLORETA was descriptive only. The single uncontrolled case is hypothesis-generating and does not establish efficacy or mechanism.

papers.title: Circadian rhythm in the atrioventricular node - in electrophysiology, contractility, metabolism, intracellular signalling and extracellular matrix
papers.summary: Using mouse and human data, this study shows a circadian rhythm in the atrioventricular node that prolongs PR interval during sleep and is largely independent of vagal tone, driven instead by a local circadian clock; Bmal1 knockout reduced the PR rhythm by ~43-52%. Molecular remodeling includes rhythms in >300 signaling molecules and ~15% of 4,186 proteins, including ion channels, with reduced L-type Ca2+ current and upstroke velocity during sleep confirmed by computer modeling.

papers.title: Postoperative hemispheric hyperperfusion and status epilepticus after chronic subdural hematoma evacuation: a case report.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 40-year-old man who developed right hemispheric hyperperfusion, neurological deterioration, generalized seizures, and refractory status epilepticus after burr-hole drainage of a chronic subdural hematoma, most consistent with probable cerebral hyperperfusion syndrome. He was managed with strict blood pressure control, antiseizure therapy, deep intravenous anesthesia, and continuous EEG, with gradual resolution and no neurological deficits at discharge and seizure freedom at 1 year.

papers.title: Intrinsic Sweetness and Sweetness-Enhancing Property of β-Damascone.
papers.summary: Combining sensory evaluation, EEG, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics with a TAS1R2-TAS1R3 model, this study found that β-damascone alone has negligible intrinsic sweetness but significantly amplifies and prolongs sucrose-induced sweetness, with strengthened cortical responses during co-stimulation. Simulations indicate β-damascone binds a peripheral region of the TAS1R2 VFD LB1-LB2 cleft, stabilizing a closed conformation and facilitating activation-associated rearrangements, supporting its potential for sugar reduction.

papers.title: Diet and Sex Influence Central Amygdala Neuroimmune Regulation of Binge Behaviors.
papers.summary: Used chemogenetic Gi-DREADD astrocyte modulation, Ca2+ imaging, and electrophysiology in male mice to show that central amygdala astrocytes exert session-proximal control over binge-like ethanol intake, and that intermittent high-fat diet plus ethanol history sensitizes CeA astrocyte Ca2+ responses and glutamatergic drive; maintenance diet and sex modulated ethanol intake and CeA IL-10/IL-13 levels.

papers.title: A Novel DHX9 Variant Was Identified in a Patient With Developmental Delay, Facial Dysmorphism and Seizure.
papers.journal: International journal of developmental neuroscience : the official journal of the International Society for Developmental Neuroscience
papers.summary: Reports a female patient with DHX9-related neurodevelopmental disorder presenting global developmental delay, ASD, facial dysmorphism, epilepsy, microcephaly, and abnormal brain MRI, carrying a likely de novo missense variant p.(His514Tyr) in the conserved DEIH helicase motif; structural modeling suggested altered hydrogen bonding and local stability, expanding the DHX9 variant phenotypic spectrum.

papers.title: Synergistic electro-mechanical stimulation promotes neural stem cell differentiation in a 3D conductive and stretchable hydrogel.
papers.summary: Developed conductive GelMA/PEGDA hydrogels incorporating PEDOT:PSS to study 3D neural stem cell differentiation under electrical stimulation and mechanical stretching; co-stimulation synergistically increased neurite outgrowth 2.5-fold versus unstimulated control, raised filopodia density and branching, upregulated GFAP/Tuj-1/MAP2, and enhanced neuronal electrical activity.

papers.title: Reducing the diagnostic odyssey in childhood-onset non-5q spinal muscular atrophy through phenotype-guided genomic evaluation.
papers.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: Argues that phenotype-guided genomic evaluation, integrating onset age, weakness distribution, reflexes, CK, electrophysiology, neuroimaging, and family history, can prioritize candidate genes and improve variant interpretation in childhood-onset non-5q spinal muscular atrophy after SMN1 exclusion, citing genotype-associated patterns such as TRPV4, ASCC1, BICD2, VRK1, and HEXB.

papers.title: Oral glycoside supplement (triterpenoid saponins) for early and intermediate stage age-related macular degeneration (SAMADI trial): study protocol for a double masked randomised placebo-controlled feasibility trial.
papers.summary: Presents the protocol for the SAMADI double-masked randomised placebo-controlled feasibility trial testing oral triterpenoid saponin supplements versus placebo for 4 months in 60 participants with early or intermediate age-related macular degeneration, with primary outcomes on recruitment, retention, adherence, acceptability, eligibility, outcome-data collection, and serious adverse events.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
